answer: Down the ropewalk the ropemaker lays strand upon strand, and the count of each rope is written in his book beside the ship it serves. A island rope claimed as laid fails the count: the strands must twist true at the relic of the rope, and a rope never laid is only loose hemp. Forging a ropewalk season means hiring a ropemaker, faking eighty counts and paying 7,600, and the wander entry in the book is read at every rigging, so a rope whose strands were never laid parts in the first gale.
